text:
sasha: FYI running into a weird failure while testing the Ruby SDK streaming client. Client retries after a 429 and the server shows the request applied twice (duplicate side effects). Anyone seen this with resume-token + retries?
maya: @sasha can you paste the exact flow? is it a single streaming request that restarts, or two distinct requests?
sasha: single client call, server returns 429 mid-stream, client backoffs and retries. When the retry hits, server processed a final chunk from the original attempt, then processed the retried request too. We expect resume_token to let us continue but it looks like the initial request committed before the retry replay. logs:

```
[2026-02-18T10:12:02Z] stream: got 429 throttle
[2026-02-18T10:12:05Z] client: retry attempt=1 backoff=200ms
[2026-02-18T10:12:05Z] server: processed final chunk id=abc123 commit=true
[2026-02-18T10:12:07Z] client: retry request with no idempotency-key
[2026-02-18T10:12:07Z] server: processed resumed stream as new request
```
sasha: ruby client doesn't automatically attach an Idempotency-Key for streaming endpoints; other lang clients add one in the transport layer. thinking this is the gap.
jon: streaming + side effects is always tricky. two orthogonal concerns: 1) server commit semantics (did server commit before responding 429?) 2) whether retry is logically a replay (idempotent) or a resume. If server commits on partial progress, retries without an idempotency key = duplicate.
lucas: we should prefer resume semantics for streaming: send resume_token and server should continue from last acked position, not reapply. But if server previously marked a chunk as committed and client didn't see it, resume must be careful.
maya: practical SDK guidance: (a) use exponential backoff with full jitter for 429/5xx, (b) always attach an Idempotency-Key header on any request that can cause side effects unless the API explicitly supports resume semantics, (c) for streaming endpoints, try resume_token first and only fall back to replay when an explicit idempotency-key exists.
jon: agree. For backoff details we use algo: base=100ms, cap=10s, attempts<=6, sleep = random_between(0, min(cap, base*2**attempt)). full jitter.
sasha: ok. For Ruby specifically, patch proposal: if current flow has resume_token in metadata, set header X-Resume-Token: <token> and don't generate Idempotency-Key; else generate Idempotency-Key per top-level request. Thoughts?
nora: server-side we can add a guard: when a resume token is presented, validate its last_applied_offset and make resume idempotent; if no resume token, treat Idempotency-Key as source of truth. Also respect Retry-After header when present.
lucas: one more: clients should honor Retry-After for polite retries. If Retry-After is present, backoff should at least wait that long before attempts; combine with exponential for subsequent attempts.
opsbot: deploy note: rolled runtime fix for resume-token validation to canary at 10:15 UTC :rocket:
sasha: thanks. I'll open a small PR in ruby-sdk to: generate idempotency-key for non-resumable streams, attach resume header when present, and implement full jitter helper matching Jon's params. Will include tests that simulate mid-stream 429 and assert single commit.
maya: ping @jon for quick review on the jitter helper and @lucas for server compatibility checklist. Also add a short snippet to the DevEx guide.
jon: happy to review, please add a unit test that asserts we use Retry-After when provided, and a property test for jitter bounds.
sasha: will do. timeline: PR by EOD today, canary tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
